messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: A problem with the nonlinear model
parts:
You can't use (eg) 'X11*X82' for a product term. In lavaan syntax, 'X11'
is used as a label.

The best approach here is to first create all those product terms (and
call them eg X11.X82) and add them to your data.frame. Then, you can use
them as any other variable.

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: A problem with the nonlinear model
parts:
I meant content-wise.

If your variables are best treated as ordered, then multiplying them doesn't make sense. For example, VarA =2 and VarB = 2 gives VarAB = 4. But so does VarA = 1 and VarB =4.  This is fine if VarA and VarB are interval, and the difference between 1 and 2 is half the difference between 2 and 4. But if you can't make that assumption, then having VarAB come out the same for the two situations may not be reasonable.

So the question is whether the gain in being able to use product terms is worth the cost of forcing ordinal variables into an interval-variable framework. That's why I asked what the variables represent, so you can think about whether that cost is worth paying in your particular situation.

Pat

You can't use (eg) 'X11*X82' for a product term. In lavaan syntax, 'X11'
is used as a label.

The best approach here is to first create all those product terms (and
call them eg X11.X82) and add them to your data.frame. Then, you can use
them as any other variable.

Yves.
